investigation.title: harness-memory-roundtrip eval failure: PUT /api/harness/agents/.../memory/facts/... returns 422 due to missing `key` field in request body
investigation.summary: The harness-memory-roundtrip eval failed with a 422 Unprocessable Entity on the fact-update step (PUT /api/harness/agents/.../memory/facts/...) because the server-side JSON deserializer rejected the request body for missing the required field `key` at byte position 48. This caused the eval probe to abort before collecting any evidence, leaving all 14 required contract fields unpopulated.
investigation.rootCause: The PUT request body sent by the eval runner to the harness memory facts endpoint is missing the required `key` field. The harness API's Rust deserializer (indicated by the serde-style error message "Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: missing field `key` at line 1 column 48") enforces `key` as a non-optional field on the fact update struct. Because the request body omits `key`, the server returns HTTP 422 before any memory operation completes, and the eval runner receives no usable evidence. This is localized to the fact-update (PUT) step of the memory roundtrip; the sibling harness-skills-roundtrip check passed cleanly in the same run, confirming the harness process itself is reachable and the agent/org setup path is functional.

possibleCauses: Most likely — The eval runner's PUT request body for the fact-update step omits the `key` field. The harness API's Rust deserialization struct requires `key` as a mandatory field; sending a body without it produces the exact 422 + serde error observed (failed-check.message). This could result from: (a) the runner constructing the update payload without a `key` property, or (b) a server-side schema change that made `key` required where it was previously optional or had a default.

Less likely — A recent server-side change to the harness memory facts API added or tightened the `key` field requirement on the PUT handler, breaking a previously valid request shape. Commit d58f85f (suspect-change.d58f85f) touched CI/workflow files and eval infrastructure files but no candidate harness API source paths were identified in its touched paths, so this is a hypothesis only and not supported by direct source evidence.

Least likely — The eval runner serializes the fact payload correctly but a middleware layer (e.g., body transformation, content-type mismatch) strips or truncates the `key` field before it reaches the deserializer. The error position 'line 1 column 48' suggests a short, structurally valid but incomplete JSON body, which is more consistent with the field never being included than with truncation.

investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-06-15T20:13:51Z with an identical 409 conflict response from POST /api/agents: "conflict: agent quota exceeded: limit is 100". The eval probe account's organization has reached the swarm agent quota ceiling, causing every attempt to create a new remote agent to be rejected before any evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) can be collected.
investigation.rootCause: The production-api swarm backend is returning HTTP 409 with error code "conflict" and message "agent quota exceeded: limit is 100" for every POST /api/agents call made by the observability probe account. Because agent creation is the first step in all three remote-agents checks (evidenced by run-status-probes.mjs line 1258 calling createAgent immediately after requireOrgId), none of the checks can proceed past the creation step, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) unpopulated. This is an eval-infrastructure failure against the production API: the probe org has exhausted its remote agent quota. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet, so a broader production outage cannot be asserted.

investigation.summary: The AURA observability eval for check process-run-lifecycle failed on desktop-nightly-macos-aarch64 when the eval runner issued POST /api/processes/[REDACTED]/trigger and received HTTP 400 with error code harness_error and message "missing model — dev loop start request must include an explicit model identifier". Because the trigger call was rejected before a run was created, zero evidence was collected and all eight required contract fields (orgId, projectId, processId, runId, runStatus, runCount, eventCount, artifactCount) are missing. This is an eval-layer failure localized to the desktop-release harness trigger path; no user-traffic or incident signals are present in the packet.
investigation.rootCause: The process trigger endpoint rejected the eval's trigger request because the harness dev loop start payload did not include a model identifier. The API enforces that a model field must be explicitly set in the trigger request body; the eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, process-run-lifecycle branch) either omitted the model field entirely or passed an empty/null value. This caused an immediate 400 before any run was created, leaving all required evidence unrecorded and failing the contract. The root cause is localized to the trigger request construction in the eval runner or to a missing/misconfigured model value in the desktop-release eval environment — not a broad API or process-workflow outage, as sibling checks process-list and process-crud both passed against the production API.

investigations.title: harness-memory-roundtrip eval failure: PUT /api/harness/agents/.../memory/facts/... returns 422 due to missing `key` field in request body
investigations.summary: The harness-memory-roundtrip eval failed with a 422 Unprocessable Entity on the fact-update step (PUT /api/harness/agents/.../memory/facts/...) because the server-side JSON deserializer rejected the request body for missing the required field `key` at byte position 48. This caused the eval probe to abort before collecting any evidence, leaving all 14 required contract fields unpopulated.
investigations.rootCause: The PUT request body sent by the eval runner to the harness memory facts endpoint is missing the required `key` field. The harness API's Rust deserializer (indicated by the serde-style error message "Failed to deserialize the JSON body into the target type: missing field `key` at line 1 column 48") enforces `key` as a non-optional field on the fact update struct. Because the request body omits `key`, the server returns HTTP 422 before any memory operation completes, and the eval runner receives no usable evidence. This is localized to the fact-update (PUT) step of the memory roundtrip; the sibling harness-skills-roundtrip check passed cleanly in the same run, confirming the harness process itself is reachable and the agent/org setup path is functional.

possibleCauses: Most likely — The eval runner's PUT request body for the fact-update step omits the `key` field. The harness API's Rust deserialization struct requires `key` as a mandatory field; sending a body without it produces the exact 422 + serde error observed (failed-check.message). This could result from: (a) the runner constructing the update payload without a `key` property, or (b) a server-side schema change that made `key` required where it was previously optional or had a default.

Less likely — A recent server-side change to the harness memory facts API added or tightened the `key` field requirement on the PUT handler, breaking a previously valid request shape. Commit d58f85f (suspect-change.d58f85f) touched CI/workflow files and eval infrastructure files but no candidate harness API source paths were identified in its touched paths, so this is a hypothesis only and not supported by direct source evidence.

Least likely — The eval runner serializes the fact payload correctly but a middleware layer (e.g., body transformation, content-type mismatch) strips or truncates the `key` field before it reaches the deserializer. The error position 'line 1 column 48' suggests a short, structurally valid but incomplete JSON body, which is more consistent with the field never being included than with truncation.

investigations.summary: The image-generation-stream eval targeting the production-api runtime environment failed immediately (2230 ms) with a SESSION_OPEN_FAILED error carrying HTTP 404, indicating the agent runtime harness endpoint resolved by LOCAL_HARNESS_URL or SWARM_BASE_URL was not reachable or returned a route-not-found response. The identical check passed on the desktop-release runtime environment in the same run window, proving the image generation pipeline itself is functional and isolating the failure to the production-api harness connectivity or configuration.
investigations.rootCause: The eval runner called /api/generate/image/stream against the production-api runtime environment and received a 404 before any generation frames could be produced. The stream emitted generation_start followed immediately by generation_error with code SESSION_OPEN_FAILED, meaning the agent runtime session could not be opened because the harness endpoint was not found at the configured URL. No frameTypes or imageUrlPresent evidence was collected as a result. This is an eval infrastructure / harness connectivity failure scoped to the production-api runtime environment; it is not evidence of a user-facing image generation outage, as the check is marked required=false with statusImpact=informational and the desktop-release sibling passed.
